- Employee benefits: The company sponsors defined contribution plans; expenses were $63.5 million (FY2020), $39.9 million (FY2019), and $39.8 million (FY2018).
text:
Fair Value Measurements:  The fair values of the Company's financial assets and financial lia bilities reflect the amounts that would be received to sell the asse ts or paid to transfer the liabilities in an
orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement dat e (exit price). The Company determines fair value based on a three-tie red fair value hierarchy. The hierarchy consists of:
• Level 1: fair value measurements represent exchange-traded securitie s which are valued at quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for ide ntical assets or liabilities that the
Company has the ability to access as of the reporting date;
• Level 2: fair value measurements are determined using input prices th at are directly observable for the asset or liability or indirectly obs ervable through corroboration with
observable market data; and
• Level 3: fair value measurements are determined using unobservable i nputs, such as internally developed pricing models for the asset or l iability due to little or no market activity
for the asset or liability.

text:
Financial Instruments:  The Company recognizes all derivative instruments on the consolidated  balance sheet at fair value. The impact on earnings from recognizing th e fair values of these
instruments depends on their intended use, their hedge designation and their effectiveness in offsetting changes in the fair values of the exposures they are hedging. Derivatives not designated as
hedging instruments are adjusted to fair value through income. Dependi ng on the nature of derivatives designated as hedging instruments, c hanges in the fair value are either offset against the change
in fair value of the hedged assets, liabilities or firm commitments t hrough earnings or recognized in shareholders’ equity through other comprehe nsive income until the hedged item is recognized.
Gains or losses, if any, related to the ineffective portion of any hedge  are recognized through earnings over the life of the hedging relationsh ip.

exchange contracts, currency swap contracts, and interest rate swap arran gements, among other derivative instruments.

Employee Benefit Plans:  The Company sponsors various defined contribution plans to which it make s contributions on behalf of employees. The expense under such pla ns was $63.5 million, $39.9
million and $39.8 million for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2020, 2019 an d 2018, respectively.
58        The Company sponsors a number of defined benefit plans that provide  benefits to current and former employees. For the company-sponsored plans,  the relevant accounting guidance requires
that management make certain assumptions relating to the long-term  rate of return on plan assets, discount rates used to determine the pre sent value of future obligations and expenses, salary inflation
rates, mortality rates and other assumptions. The Company believes th at the accounting estimates related to its pension plans are cri tical accounting estimates because they are highly susceptib le to
change from period to period based on the performance of plan assets, actu arial valuations, market conditions and contracted benefit changes. Th e selection of assumptions is based on historical
trends and known economic and market conditions at the time of valuat ion, as well as independent studies of trends performed by the Company ’s actuaries. However, actual results may differ
substantially from the estimates that were based on the critical assumptions.
        The Company recognizes the funded status of each defined benefit  pension plan in the consolidated balance sheet. Each overfunded  plan is recognized as an asset and each underfunded plan is
recognized as a liability. Pension plan liabilities are revalued annua lly, or when an event occurs that requires remeasurement, based on update d assumptions and information about the individuals
covered by the plan. Accumulated actuarial gains and losses in excess of a 10 percent corridor and the prior service cost are amortized on a strai ght-line basis from the date recognized over the
average remaining service period of active participants or over the avera ge life expectancy for plans with significant inactive participants. T he service costs related to defined benefits are included in
operating income. The other components of net benefit cost other than  service cost are recorded within other non-operating income (loss), net in the consolidated statement of income

title: Equity Method Investments
heading: Equity Method Investments:
start_phrase: Investments in ordinary shares of companies, in which the Company belie ves it exercises significant influence over operating and financial p olicies, are accounted for using the equity method of accounting.
summary:
- Pension and postretirement benefits: The company sponsors defined benefit plans and deems related accounting estimates critical due to sensitivity to assumptions (long-term asset returns, discount rates, salary inflation, mortality, market conditions, actuarial valuations, and plan changes). Funded status is recognized on the balance sheet (overfunded as assets, underfunded as liabilities). Liabilities are remeasured annually or upon triggering events. Actuarial gains/losses beyond a 10% corridor and prior service costs are amortized straight-line over the average remaining service period or life expectancy for plans with many inactive participants. Service cost is in operating income; other components of net benefit cost are in other non-operating income (loss), net.
- Equity method investments: Investments with significant influence are accounted for under the equity method (cost adjusted for share of earnings/losses). Other-than-temporary impairments reset the cost basis and are not reversed. The company recorded impairment losses on its AMVIG Holdings Limited investment in each of the last three fiscal years.
- Share-based compensation: For awards with service or market conditions, expense is recognized straight-line over the vesting period using grant-date fair value and estimated forfeitures. For performance condition awards, vesting probability is reassessed each reporting period with cost adjusted accordingly. Cash-settled awards are liability-classified and remeasured to fair value each reporting period. Forfeiture estimates consider employee level, economic conditions, time to vest, and historical experience.
- Income taxes: The company applies the asset and liability method, recognizing deferred taxes for temporary differences and using enacted rates. Tax expense differs from current taxes payable due to timing differences. Deferred tax assets (including loss and credit carryforwards) are reduced by valuation allowances when realization is not more likely than not. The company evaluates and records uncertain tax positions under the prescribed recognition and measurement guidance, and records related interest and penalties as tax expense.
text:
Equity Method Investments: Investments in ordinary shares of companies, in which the Company belie ves it exercises significant influence over operating and financial p olicies, are accounted for
using the equity method of accounting. Under this method, the investment  is carried at cost and is adjusted to recognize the investor’s sha re of earnings or losses of the investee after the date of
acquisition and is adjusted for impairment whenever it is determine d that a decline in the fair value below the cost basis is other tha n temporary. The fair value of the investment then becomes the
new cost basis of the investment and it is not adjusted for subsequen t recoveries in fair value. Impairment losses have been recognized for t he Company's equity investment in AMVIG Holdings
Limited ("AMVIG") in the last three fiscal years. See Note 7, "Equity Me thod Investments," for more information regarding the Company's equity me thod investments.

title: Share-based Compensation
heading: Share-based Compensation:
start_phrase: Amcor has a variety of equity incentive plans.
summary:
- Pension and postretirement benefits: The company’s defined benefit plans rely on critical assumptions (long-term asset returns, discount rates, salary inflation, mortality) that can materially affect results. Funded status is recognized on the balance sheet (overfunded as assets, underfunded as liabilities). Liabilities are remeasured annually or upon triggering events. Actuarial gains/losses beyond a 10% corridor and prior service costs are amortized straight-line over participants’ average remaining service or life expectancy. Service cost is in operating income; other net benefit components are in other non-operating income (loss).

- Equity method investments: Holdings with significant influence are accounted for under the equity method (cost adjusted for share of investee results). Other-than-temporary impairments reset the cost basis and are not reversed. The company has recognized recent impairments on its AMVIG Holdings Limited investment.

- Share-based compensation: For awards with service or market conditions, expense is recognized straight-line over the vesting period using grant-date fair value and estimated vesting. For performance conditions, vesting probability is reassessed each period with cost adjusted accordingly. Cash-settled awards are liability-classified and remeasured to fair value each reporting period. Forfeiture rates are estimated based on role, economic factors, time to vest, and history.

- Income taxes: The asset-liability method is used, recording deferred taxes for temporary differences and carryforwards using enacted rates. Tax expense differs from current payable due to timing differences. Deferred tax assets may be reduced by valuation allowances when realization is not more likely than not. Uncertain tax positions are evaluated under prescribed recognition/measurement guidance, with related interest and penalties recorded in the tax provision.
text:
Share-based Compensation:  Amcor has a variety of equity incentive plans. For employee awards with a serv ice or market condition, compensation expense is recognized over the ves ting period on
a straight-line basis using the grant date fair value of the award and the es timated number of awards that are expected to vest. For awards with a perform ance condition, the Company must reassess
the probability of vesting at each reporting period and adjust compen sation cost based on its probability assessment. The Company als o has cash-settled share-based compensation plans which are
accounted for as liabilities. Such share-based awards are remeasured t o fair value at each reporting period. The Company estimates forfeitures b ased on employee level, economic conditions, time
remaining to vest and historical forfeiture experience.

title: Income Taxes
heading: Income Taxes:
start_phrase: The Company uses the asset and liability method to account for incom e taxes.
summary:
- Defined benefit pension plans: Treatment relies on critical estimates (expected return on assets, discount rate, salary inflation, mortality and other actuarial assumptions). Funded status is recognized on the balance sheet (overfunded as assets, underfunded as liabilities). Plans are remeasured annually or upon triggering events. Actuarial gains/losses beyond a 10% corridor and prior service costs are amortized on a straight-line basis over average remaining service periods (or life expectancy for plans with many inactive participants). Service cost is in operating income; other net benefit cost components are in other non-operating income (loss), net.

- Equity method investments: Used when the Company has significant influence. Investments are carried at cost and adjusted for the Company’s share of post-acquisition earnings/losses. Other-than-temporary impairments reset the cost basis with no reversal for later recoveries. Recent impairments have been recognized for the AMVIG investment (see Note 7).

- Share-based compensation: For awards with service or market conditions, expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the vesting period using grant-date fair value and estimated forfeitures. For performance-condition awards, vesting probability is reassessed each period with corresponding cost adjustments. Cash-settled awards are treated as liabilities and remeasured to fair value each reporting period. Forfeiture estimates consider employee level, economic conditions, time to vest, and historical experience.

- Income taxes: Applies the asset-liability method. Deferred taxes arise from differences between tax bases and financial reporting amounts using enacted laws/rates; tax expense differs from current payable due to timing differences. Deferred tax assets (including loss and credit carryforwards) are reduced by a valuation allowance when realization is not more likely than not. The Company evaluates and records uncertain tax positions under prescribed recognition and measurement guidance; interest and penalties are recorded as tax expense (see Note 16).
text:
Income Taxes:  The Company uses the asset and liability method to account for incom e taxes. Deferred income taxes reflect the future tax consequences o f differences between the tax bases of assets
and liabilities and their financial reporting amounts at each balanc e sheet date, based upon enacted income tax laws and tax rates. In come tax expense or benefit is provided based on earnings reported
in the consolidated financial statements. The provision for incom e tax expense or benefit differs from the amounts of income taxes currently  payable because certain items of income and expense
included in the consolidated financial statements are recognized in d ifferent time periods by taxing authorities.
        Deferred tax assets, including operating loss, capital loss and ta x credit carryforwards, are reduced by a valuation allowance when, in the opin ion of management, it is more likely than not that
any portion of these tax attributes will not be realized. In addition, fro m time to time, management must assess the need to accrue or disclo se uncertain tax positions for proposed adjustments from
various tax authorities who regularly audit the Company in the normal course  of business. In making these assessments, management must oft en analyze complex tax laws of multiple jurisdictions.
Accounting guidance prescribes a recognition threshold and measurement  attribute for the financial statement recognition and measurement  of a tax position taken or expected to be taken in a tax
return. The Company records the related interest expense and penalties, i f any, as tax expense in the tax provision. See Note 16, "Income Taxes,"  for more information on the Company's income
taxes.

summary:
- Overview of Note 3 summarizing newly adopted and pending accounting standards and their effects on the company’s financial statements and disclosures.

Recently adopted:
- SEC Rule 33-10762 (guarantor/issuer disclosures under Regulation S-X Rule 3-10): early adopted in Q3 FY2020; replaces condensed consolidating financials with summarized financial information presented in MD&A.
- FASB guidance on releasing income tax effects from AOCI (post–Tax Cuts and Jobs Act): adopted 7/1/2019; company did not elect optional reclassification; impact not material.

  - Lease expense not expected to change materially; enhanced lease disclosures begin in FY2020 (see Note 14).

Not yet adopted:
- CECL (credit losses on financial assets): effective 7/1/2020; to be adopted using modified retrospective approach; not expected to be material.
- ASU 2019-12 (income taxes simplification): effective 7/1/2021; impact under evaluation.
- ASC 848 (reference rate reform for LIBOR transition): optional expedients issued March 2020; election under evaluation.
- All other not-yet-adopted ASUs deemed not applicable or expected to have minimal impact.
text:
Recently Adopted Accounting Standards
        In March 2020, the SEC issued Final Rule Release No. 33-10762, " Financial Disclosures About Guarantors and Issuers of Guarante ed Securities and Affiliates Whose Securities Collateralize  a
Registrant's Securities " that simplifies the disclosure requirements related to registere d securities under Rule 3-10 of Regulation S-X. The rule replaces the require ment to provide condensed
consolidating financial information with a requirement to present sum marized financial information of the issuers and guarantors in eithe r a note to the financial statements or in management's
discussion and analysis. The effective date of the amendment is Ja nuary 4, 2021 with earlier voluntary compliance permitted. The Company  elected to adopt the amended rules effective with our third
fiscal quarter of 2020 and has included the required disclosures as a comp onent of "Part II, Item 7. - Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" of this
Annual Report on Form 10-K.
        In February 2018, the Financial Accounting Standards Board ("FASB") issued g uidance that requires the Company to disclose a description of the  Company’s accounting policy for releasing
income tax effects from accumulated other comprehensive income an d whether the Company elects to reclassify the stranded income tax ef fects from the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act ("The Act"), along
with information about other income tax effects that are reclassified. For all entities, the guidance was effective for fiscal years beginning  after December 15, 2018 and interim periods within those
fiscal years. Entities can choose whether to apply the amendments retro spectively to each period in which the effect of the Act is recogniz ed or to apply the amendments in the period of adoption.
This guidance was effective for the Company on July 1, 2019. The Company adopted the new guidance effective July 1, 2019 and did not elect th e optional reclassification as the impact was not
material.
        In August 2017, the FASB issued guidance which simplifies existing g uidance in order to allow companies to more accurately present the  economic effects of risk management activities in the
financial statements. For public business entities, the amendm ents in Accounting Standards Update ("ASU") 2017-12 were effective for financ ial statements issued for fiscal years beginning after
December 15, 2018 and interim periods within those fiscal years. Thi s guidance was effective for the Company on July 1, 2019 using the modi fied retrospective approach, with the exception of
presentation and disclosure guidance which is adopted prospective ly. Implementation of the standard did not have a material impact on  the Company's condensed consolidated financial statements.
        In February 2016, the FASB issued guidance that required lessees to put mos t leases on their balance sheets but recognize expenses on their in come statements in a manner similar to past
accounting guidance. The guidance also eliminates the previo us real estate-specific provisions and changes the guidance on sa le-leaseback transactions, initial direct costs and lease execu tory costs
for all entities. Lease classification will determine how to recog nize lease-related revenue and expense. The Company adopted the new l ease standard at July 1, 2019 using a simplified transition
option that allows for a cumulative-effect adjustment in the period  of adoption and therefore did not restate prior periods. The Company also  elected to adopt the package of practical expedients
which allows for existing operating leases to continue to be class ified as operating leases under the new guidance without reassessing whether the contracts contain a lease under the new guidance or
whether classification of the operating lease would be different under the  new standard. The Company did not elect the use-of-hindsight practi cal expedient but did adopt the practical expedient
pertaining to land easements which provides the option not to reas sess whether land easements not previously accounted for as leases unde r prior leasing guidance would be leases under the new
guidance.
        Adoption of the new leasing standard resulted in the following impa cts to the Company's condensed consolidated financial statements as  of the adoption date: the establishment of a lease liability
of $590.5 million, including current portion, a corresponding right-of-use as set of $569.8 million, and the reclassification of approximately $58.2 m illion (net of tax) of deferred gains on sale
leaseback transactions.

Accounting Standards Not Yet Adopted
        In June 2016, the FASB issued guidance which requires financial assets , or a group of financial assets measured at amortized cost basis to b e presented at the net amount expected to be collected
when finalized. The allowance for credit losses is a valuation accou nt that will be deducted from the amortized cost basis of the financ ial asset to present the net carrying value at the amount expected
to be collected on the financial asset. This guidance affects lo ans, debt securities, trade receivables, net investments in lease s, off-balance-sheet credit exposures, reinsurance receivables and any ot her
financial assets not excluded from the scope that have the contract ual right to receive cash. For public business entities, the amendm ents in this update are effective for fiscal years beginning after
December 15, 2019, including interim periods within those fiscal years. The  guidance will be effective for the Company on July 1, 2020 and will be  adopted using the modified retrospective
approach. The Company does not expect the standard to have a materi al impact on its consolidated financial statements.
        In December 2019, the FASB issued updated guidance to simplify the ac counting for income taxes by removing certain exceptions and improving th e consistent application of U.S. GAAP in
other tax accounting areas. This guidance is effective for annual rep orting periods, and any interim periods within those annual perio ds, that begin after December 15, 2020 with early adoption
permitted. Accordingly, the guidance will be effective for the Compan y on July 1, 2021. The Company is currently evaluating the impact th at this guidance will have on its financial statements and
related disclosures.
        In March 2020, the FASB issued optional expedients and exceptions t o ease the potential burden in accounting for reference rate reform rela ted to contract modifications, hedging relationships,
and other transactions that reference the London Interbank Offered Rate ("LIBO R") or another reference rate expected to be discontinued, subject to  meeting certain criteria. The Company is
currently evaluating whether to elect the adoption of this optional  guidance.
        The Company considers the applicability and impact of a ll ASUs issued by the FASB and SEC. The Company determined that all other ASUs not yet adopted to be either not applicable or are
expected to have minimal impact on the Company's consolidated fin ancial statements at this time.

Note 5 - Discontinued Operations

title: 2019 Bemis Integration Plan
heading: 2019 Bemis Integration Plan
start_phrase: In connection with the acquisition of Bemis, the Company initiat ed restructuring activities in the fourth quarter of 2019 aimed at integ rating and optimizing the combined organization.
summary:
- Overview of multiple restructuring initiatives detailing objectives, timelines, costs, cash outflows, and status across segments (Flexibles, Rigid Packaging, and Corporate), including distinctions between restructuring-related and general integration costs.

- 2019 Bemis Integration Plan:
  - Initiated post-Bemis acquisition (Q4 2019) to integrate and optimize the combined organization.
  - Targeting approximately $180 million of pre-tax synergies by end of fiscal 2022 from procurement, supply chain, and G&A savings.
  - Total estimated integration costs of about $200 million: $165 million restructuring and related, $35 million general integration.
  - Restructuring/related breakdown: ~$90 million employee-related, $25 million fixed asset-related, $20 million other restructuring, $30 million restructuring-related.
  - About $150 million expected cash outlay (including $115 million tied to restructuring/related).
  - FY2020 cash payments were $80.2 million, with $54.1 million for restructuring/related.
  - Applies to the Flexibles segment and Corporate; completion expected by end of fiscal 2022.
  - Clarifies that restructuring-related costs are directly tied to the activities (e.g., facility closures, graphics replacement, training on relocated equipment) but do not qualify for exit/disposal accounting; general integration costs are separate.

- 2018 Rigid Packaging Restructuring Plan:
  - Announced August 21, 2018 to reduce structural costs and optimize the manufacturing footprint via facility closures and headcount reductions, driving productivity and overhead savings.
  - Expected total pre-tax restructuring costs of ~$110 million, increased by ~$15 million in Q4 FY2020 due to additional non-cash impairments.
  - Estimated $65–$70 million in cash outflows; FY2020 cash payments were $23.6 million.
  - Expected completion in fiscal 2021.

- 2016 Flexibles Restructuring Plan:
  - Announced June 9, 2016 to optimize cost base and support earnings growth in Flexibles through footprint optimization, capacity alignment, higher utilization, and organizational streamlining (particularly in Europe).
  - Actions included closing eight manufacturing facilities and reducing headcount.
  - Total pre-tax restructuring costs of $230.8 million: $166.7 million employee termination, $31.4 million fixed asset impairments, $32.7 million other costs (equipment dismantling, lease terminations).
  - Approximately $166 million resulted in cash expenditures; FY2019 cash payments were $14.4 million.
  - Substantially completed by end of fiscal 2019.

- Other Restructuring Plans:
  - Individually immaterial plans with restructuring charges of approximately $17.9 million (FY2020), $18.8 million (FY2019), and $25.8 million (FY2018).
text:
2019 Bemis Integration Plan
        In connection with the acquisition of Bemis, the Company initiat ed restructuring activities in the fourth quarter of 2019 aimed at integ rating and optimizing the combined organization. As
previously announced, the Company continues to target realizing app roximately $180 million of pre-tax synergies driven by procurement, suppl y chain, and general and administrative savings by the
end of fiscal year 2022.
        The Company's total 2019 Bemis Integration Plan pre-tax integra tion costs are expected to be approximately $200 million. The tota l 2019 Bemis Integration Plan costs include $165 million of
restructuring and related expenses and $35 million of general integra tion expenses. The restructuring and related expenses are comprised  of approximately $90 million in employee related expenses,
$25 million in fixed asset related expenses, $20 million in other re structuring and $30 million in restructuring related expenses. The C ompany estimates that approximately $150 million of the $200
million total integration costs will result in cash expenditures, o f which $115 million relate to restructuring and related expenditures. Ca sh payments for the fiscal year 2020 were $80.2 million, of
which $54.1 million were payments related to restructuring and relat ed expenditures. The 2019 Bemis Integration Plan relates to the Flexible s segment and Corporate and is expected to be completed
by the end of fiscal year 2022.
        Restructuring related costs are directly attributable to restruc turing activities; however, they do not qualify for special accounting treatment as exit or disposal activities. General integration cos ts
are not linked to restructuring. The Company believes the disclosure  of restructuring related costs provides more information on the total cost  of our 2019 Bemis Integration Plan. The restructuring
related costs relate primarily to the closure of facilities and inclu de costs to replace graphics and train new employees on relocated equi pment.

Holdings Limited ("AMVIG") of 47.6% and other individually immaterial in vestments.
        AMVIG is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Its quoted share price as of June 30, 2020 and 2019 was $0.18 (HKD 1.40) and $0.24 (HKD 1.85), respectiv ely. The value of Amcor's

other-than-temporary impairment of $25.6 million, $14.0 million and $3 6.5 million, respectively, to bring the value of its investment to fair value. The impairment charge was included in equity in

In addition to assets and liabilities that are recorded at fair val ue on a recurring basis, the Company records assets and liabilities at fair value on a nonrecurring basis as required by U.S. GAAP.
The Company measures certain assets, including the Company’s equit y method investments, technology intangible assets, other intangib le assets and goodwill at fair value on a nonrecurring basis
when they are deemed to be other than temporarily impaired. The fair val ues of these assets are determined, when applicable, based on val uation techniques using the best information available, and
may include quoted market prices, market comparables and discounted  cash flow projections.
        The Company tests for impairment of its equity method investments  when impairment indicators are present. Impairment tests were performed by comparing the carrying value of the
Company’s investment in AMVIG at the end of each
73period, including interim periods, to the fair value of the investmen t, which was determined based on AMVIG's quoted share price which is cl assified in Level 1 of the fair value hierarchy.

start_phrase: The Company periodically uses derivatives and other financial inst ruments to hedge exposures to interest rates, commodity and currency risk s.
summary:
Derivative Instruments
        The Company periodically uses derivatives and other financial inst ruments to hedge exposures to interest rates, commodity and currency risk s. The Company does not hold or issue financial
instruments for speculative or trading purposes. For hedges that meet the hedge accounting criteria, the Company, at inception, formally desig nates and documents the instrument as a fair value hedge
or a cash flow hedge of a specific underlying exposure. On an ongoing basis, th e Company assesses and documents that its hedges have been and are ex pected to continue to be highly effective.

title: Interest Rate Risk
heading: Interest Rate Risk
start_phrase: The Company's policy is to manage exposure to interest rate risk by maintaining a mixture of fixed-rate and variable-rate debt, monitori ng global interest rates and, where appropriate, hedging floating interest rate exposure or debt at fixed interest rates through various interest rate derivative instruments including, but not limited to, i nterest rate swaps, cross-currency interest rate swaps, and interest rate locks.
summary:
- Scope: Company’s use of derivative and other financial instruments to hedge interest rate, commodity, and foreign currency risks; no speculative trading; formal hedge designation and ongoing effectiveness assessments for qualifying hedges.
- Interest rate risk management:
  - Strategy: Maintain mix of fixed and variable debt; hedge via interest rate swaps, cross-currency interest rate swaps, and interest rate locks.
  - Accounting:
    - Fair value hedges: Changes in fair value of swaps and the hedged debt recognized in interest expense.
    - Non-designated swaps: Fair value changes recognized in other non-operating income (loss), net.
  - Volumes:
    - Receive-fixed/pay-variable interest rate swaps outstanding: $837.1 million at June 30, 2020 ($841.1 million at June 30, 2019).
    - Cross-currency interest rate swaps outstanding: $100 million (€89.0 million) at June 30, 2020; not designated, changes recognized in earnings.
  - Treasury locks:
    - Entered six Treasury lock agreements in Q3 FY2020 (notional $250.0 million) as cash flow hedges of anticipated long-term debt issuance; deemed highly effective.
    - Upon issuing unsecured senior notes on June 19, 2020, settled locks with $19.8 million cash payment; loss recorded in AOCI and amortized to interest expense over the 10-year note life.
- Foreign currency risk management:
  - Strategy: Hedge exchange rate volatility using forward contracts; manage net investment exposure primarily via borrowings in relevant currencies.
  - Accounting:
    - Cash flow hedges: Effective portion of forward contracts’ fair value changes to AOCI and reclassified to earnings when hedged transactions occur; ineffective portion to earnings in the same line item as the hedged item.
    - Non-designated forwards: Fair value changes recognized in the consolidated statement of income.
    - Net investment hedges: Effective remeasurement gains/losses on designated external borrowings to AOCI; ineffectiveness to other non-operating income (loss), net.
  - Volumes: Outstanding forward contract notional amounts of $1.6 billion at June 30, 2020 ($1.0 billion at June 30, 2019).
text:
Interest Rate Risk
        The Company's policy is to manage exposure to interest rate risk by maintaining a mixture of fixed-rate and variable-rate debt, monitori ng global interest rates and, where appropriate, hedging
floating interest rate exposure or debt at fixed interest rates through various  interest rate derivative instruments including, but not limited to, i nterest rate swaps, cross-currency interest rate swaps, and
interest rate locks.
        For interest rate swaps that are accounted for as fair value hedges, cha nges in the fair value of both the hedging instruments and the underlying  debt obligations are immediately recognized in
interest expense. Changes in the fair value of interest rate swaps tha t have not been designated as hedging instruments are reported in the a ccompanying consolidated statement of income under other
non-operating income (loss), net.
        As of June 30, 2020 and 2019, the total notional amount of the Company 's receive-fixed/pay-variable interest rate swaps was $837.1 million and  $841.1 million, respectively.
        At June 30, 2020, the Company had a notional amount of $100 million  (equivalent to €89.0 million) cross-currency interest rate swaps outsta nding. The Company did not designate the swaps as
a hedging instrument and thus changes in fair value were immediatel y recognized in earnings.
        During the third quarter of fiscal year 2020, the Company entered into six  Treasury lock agreements to protect against unfavorable interest rate  changes relating to the highly probable issuance of
long-term debt. The total notional amount of the Treasury lock of $250. 0 million was designated as a cash flow hedge of an anticipated trans action and deemed these agreements to be highly
effective.
        The associated unsecured senior note was issued on June 19, 2020 , and the Company has settled these Treasury lock agreements with a  $19.8 million cash payment to the counterparties. The loss
associated with the settlement was recorded in accumulated other c omprehensive loss and will be amortized to interest expense over th e life of the unsecured senior notes, which is 10 years.

title: Foreign Currency Risk
heading: Foreign Currency Risk
start_phrase: The Company manufactures and sells its products and finances opera tions in a number of countries throughout the world and, as a result, is exp osed to movements in foreign currency exchange rates.
summary:
- Overview: Note describes the Company’s use of derivative and other financial instruments exclusively for hedging interest rate, foreign currency, and commodity risks. Hedges are formally designated as fair value or cash flow hedges when qualifying, with ongoing effectiveness assessments. Non‑hedge (non-designated) derivatives’ fair value changes are recognized in earnings.

- Interest rate risk:
  - Strategy: Maintain a mix of fixed- and variable-rate debt; use interest rate swaps, cross-currency interest rate swaps, and interest rate locks.
  - Accounting:
    - Fair value hedges: Changes in fair value of swaps and the hedged debt are recognized in interest expense.
    - Non-designated swaps: Fair value changes recognized in other non-operating income (loss), net.
  - Activity/positions:
    - Receive-fixed/pay-variable interest rate swaps notional: $837.1 million (June 30, 2020) vs. $841.1 million (2019).
    - Cross-currency interest rate swaps notional: $100 million (€89.0 million) outstanding at June 30, 2020; not designated, changes recognized in earnings.
    - Treasury locks: Six agreements totaling $250.0 million designated as cash flow hedges for anticipated long-term debt. Upon issuing 10-year unsecured senior notes on June 19, 2020, the locks were settled with a $19.8 million cash payment; loss recorded in AOCI and to be amortized to interest expense over the notes’ life.

- Foreign currency risk:
  - Strategy: Hedge exchange rate volatility arising from global manufacturing, sales, and financing via forward contracts.
  - Accounting:
    - Cash flow hedges: Effective portions to AOCI and reclassified to earnings when hedged transactions affect results; ineffective portions to earnings. Non-designated forwards’ fair value changes recognized in earnings.
  - Activity/positions:
    - Outstanding forward contract notional: $1.6 billion (June 30, 2020) vs. $1.0 billion (2019).
    - Net investment hedges: Use borrowings in local currencies; effective portions to AOCI, ineffective to other non-operating income (loss). Upon disposal of the hedged net investment, related AOCI amounts are reclassified to earnings.
    - Commercial paper: $67.0 million designated as a net investment hedge at the start of FY2020; settled during the quarter ended December 31, 2019. Related AOCI balances remain until sale or liquidation of the subsidiaries. No net investment hedges outstanding at June 30, 2020.

- Commodity risk:
  - Exposure: Raw materials subject to price volatility (e.g., weather, supply, political/economic factors).
  - Strategy: Minimize volatility by passing commodity price risk to customers, including use of fixed-price swaps purchased on customers’ behalf; centrally managed and cash-settled at maturity with costs/benefits passed through to customers.
  - Accounting: Changes in fair value of commodity hedges recognized in AOCI; cumulative hedge amounts recognized in earnings when the forecast transaction occurs.
  - Outstanding commodity contracts:
    - Aluminum: 44,944 tons (June 30, 2020) vs. 29,342 tons (2019).
    - PET resin: 26,006,000 lbs (June 30, 2020); not applicable in 2019.
text:
Foreign Currency Risk
        The Company manufactures and sells its products and finances opera tions in a number of countries throughout the world and, as a result, is exp osed to movements in foreign currency exchange
rates. The purpose of the Company's foreign currency hedging program is to  manage the volatility associated with the changes in exchange ra tes.
        To manage this exchange rate risk, the Company utilizes forward c ontracts. Contracts that qualify for hedge accounting are designated as c ash flow hedges of certain forecasted transactions
denominated in foreign currencies. The effective portion of the changes in fair value of these instruments is reported in accumulated other comp rehensive income (loss) ("AOCI") and reclassified into
earnings in the same financial statement line item and in the same  period or periods during which the related hedged transactions affect  earnings. The ineffective portion is recognized in earnings over
the life of the hedging relationship in the same consolidated stateme nt of income line item as the underlying hedged item. Changes in th e fair value of forward contracts that have not been designated
as hedging instruments are reported in the accompanying consolida ted statement of income.
        As of June 30, 2020 and 2019, the notional amount of the outstanding forwa rd contracts was $1.6 billion and $1.0 billion, respectively.
        The Company manages its currency exposure related to the net ass ets of its foreign operations primarily through borrowings denominated in the relevant currency. Foreign currency gains and
losses from the remeasurement of external borrowings designated as net  investment hedges of a foreign operation are recognized in AOCI, to the ext ent that the hedge is effective. The ineffective
portion is immediately recognized in other non-operating income (loss),  net in the consolidated
75statement of income. When a hedged net investment is disposed of, a pe rcentage of the cumulative amount recognized in AOCI in relation to the hedged net investment is recognized in the condensed
consolidated statement of income as part of the profit or loss on disposal .
        At the beginning of fiscal year 2020, the carrying value of commercia l paper issued which is designated as a net investment hedge was $67.0  million. During the three months ended December
31, 2019, the Company settled $67.0 million of U.S. commercial paper issue d by a non-U.S. entity, which was previously designated as a net investmen t hedge in its U.S. subsidiaries. The net
investment hedges recorded through the point of settlement are included  in AOCI and will be reclassified into earnings only upon the sale or liqui dation of the related subsidiaries. The Company did
not have any net investment hedges in place as of June 30, 2020.

Swaps are cash-settled at maturity; hedge fair value changes go to AOCI and are reclassified to income when the forecast transaction occurs.
- Outstanding commodity hedges: As of June 30, 2020—Aluminum 44,944 tons (vs. 29,342 tons in 2019); PET resin 26,006,000 lbs (N/A in 2019).
- Derivative assets and liabilities (balance sheet): Total derivative assets $39.8m and liabilities $23.7m at June 30, 2020. Instruments include commodity contracts and FX forwards in cash flow hedges; interest rate swaps in fair value hedges; and non-designated FX forwards and cross-currency interest rate swaps. Current and non-current balances are presented separately; no balance offsetting elected despite netting arrangements.

- AOCI and income effects—cash flow hedges: Reclassifications from AOCI to income in 2020 totaled a $6.9m loss (primarily commodity contracts and FX forwards; includes treasury locks to interest expense).

text:
Commodity Risk
        Certain raw materials used in the Company's production processes a re subject to price volatility caused by weather, supply conditions,  political and economic variables and other unpredictable
factors. The Company's policy is to minimize exposure to price vol atility by passing through the commodity price risk to customers, including the use of fixed price swaps. The Company purchases

summary:
- Overview: Note 12 details the Company’s defined benefit pension and other post-retirement plans, encompassing both funded and unfunded arrangements across multiple countries. In FY2020, the Company maintained 21 statutory/mandated defined benefit arrangements and 57 voluntary defined benefit plans (many closed to new entrants).

- Plan structure by country and status:
  - United Kingdom: 2 funded plans, closed to new entrants.
  - Switzerland: 1 funded plan, open to new entrants.

- Facility usage and liquidity:

title: Income Taxes
heading: Note 16 - Income Taxes
start_phrase: Amcor plc is a tax resident of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland ("UK").
summary:
- Scope: Note 16 – Income Taxes for Amcor plc, a UK tax resident (prior to the Bemis acquisition, parent was Australian). Covers income before tax, tax expense, effective tax rates and reconciliations, deferred taxes, valuation allowances, carryforwards, indefinite reinvestment, uncertain tax positions, audit status, and Swiss Tax Reform impacts.
- Income before taxes: Split between domestic (UK) and foreign for fiscal years 2020, 2019, 2018; foreign operations generated the majority of pretax income.
- Income tax expense: Presented by current and deferred components, split domestic/foreign for 2020–2018.
- Tax rate reconciliation: Reconciles to statutory rates of 18.5% (UK, 2020), 19% (UK, 2019), and 30% (Australia, 2018). Key drivers include foreign tax rate differentials, non-deductible expenses, tax law changes, valuation allowance changes, and other items.
- Effective tax rates: 22.6% (2020), 28.4% (2019), 16.4% (2018). 2020 reflects a benefit from Swiss tax law changes largely offset by current-period true-ups; higher than UK statutory rate due to earnings in higher-tax jurisdictions outside the UK.
- Deferred taxes: Details of deferred tax assets (inventories, employee benefits, provisions, NOLs, credits, other accruals) and liabilities (PPE, intangible assets including Swiss reform impacts, receivables, derivatives, undistributed foreign earnings). Net deferred tax liability was $537.0m at June 30, 2020 (vs. $820.8m in 2019).
- Valuation allowance: Increased by $72.9m in 2020 (also increased in 2019 and 2018), primarily due to the deferred tax asset arising from Swiss Tax Reform; methodology nets the Swiss DTA against intangible-related DTL with a valuation allowance to amounts more-likely-than-not realizable.
- Undistributed earnings: Decrease in DTL for undistributed foreign earnings in 2020 includes $82.5m tax impact from the EC Remedy sale. About $968.2m of foreign subsidiary earnings are indefinitely reinvested; a cumulative DTL of $26.9m recorded for amounts no longer indefinitely reinvested; remaining undistributed earnings can be repatriated at no tax cost.
- Carryforwards: As of June 30, 2020, UK NOLs and credits (tax effected) of ~$2.9m with no expiry; non-UK NOLs and other attributes of ~$50.9m (majority no expiry), with valuation allowances recorded; utilization depends on future taxable income in relevant jurisdictions.
- Uncertain tax positions: Unrecognized tax benefits of $101.1m (2020) and $102.6m (2019), all of which would favorably impact the ETR if recognized. Interest and penalties accrued were $7.1m (2020), $13.8m (2019), $2.9m (2018). Rollforward provided (additions, reductions, settlements, acquisitions).
- Audits and exposure: Open tax years include US federal (2016–2019), HMRC (2019), and various US states and non-US jurisdictions (2011–2019). Reserves considered adequate, but outcomes could materially impact results or cash flows.
- Swiss Tax Reform: Swiss law changes in 2020 removed certain regimes and introduced new measures. In Q4 2020, Amcor recorded a net $21.7m benefit from an allowed step-up of intangible assets for tax purposes, recognized through reduced deferred tax expense and reflected within intangible-related deferred tax balances with an associated valuation allowance.

title: Earnings Per Share Computations
heading: Note 18 - Earnings Per Share Computations
start_phrase: The Company applies the two-class method when computing its e arnings per share ("EPS"), which requires that net income per share for each c lass of share be calculated assuming all of the Company's net income is distributed as dividends to each class of share based on their contractual rights.
summary:
- Note 18 explains the Company’s earnings per share (EPS) methodology, using the two-class method that allocates net income to each class of shares based on contractual rights.
- Basic EPS excludes ordinary shares subject to forward repurchase and is calculated from net income available to ordinary shareholders divided by the weighted-average basic shares.
- Diluted EPS reflects potentially dilutive securities (share options, restricted shares, performance rights/shares, and share rights) when dilutive.
- Detailed EPS data are presented for fiscal years 2020, 2019, and 2018, including:
  - Numerators: net income attributable to Amcor plc, adjustments for earnings attributable to shares to be repurchased, and splits between continuing and discontinued operations.
  - Denominators: weighted-average shares outstanding, reductions for shares to be repurchased, and the effect of dilutive shares.
  - Per-share results for basic and diluted EPS, showing modest dilution and small losses from discontinued operations in 2020.
- Certain stock awards were anti-dilutive and excluded from diluted EPS: 36.9 million (2020), 5.6 million (2019), and 10.3 million (2018).

- Note 19 addresses contingencies and legal proceedings.
- Brazil tax contingencies: Ongoing governmental assessments and litigation mainly related to excise and income taxes; the Company intends to defend vigorously and does not expect a material impact. Accruals recorded were $11.9 million (2020) and $16.4 million (2019), with reasonably possible losses in excess of accruals of $18.4 million (2020) and $23.7 million (2019). Collateral posted as of June 30, 2020 included $34.0 million in letters of credit, $0.9 million in judicial insurance, and $10.1 million in cash deposits.
- Environmental contingencies: The Company is a potentially responsible party at several U.S. waste sites and has recorded $17.1 million for estimated remediation at these sites, plus $46.6 million for other global remediation obligations. Insurance may not fully cover exposures; however, management does not expect a material adverse effect on liquidity, results, or financial condition.
- Legal proceedings related to the Amcor–Bemis transaction:
  - An appraisal action funded by Burford Capital on behalf of two funds contesting the merger exchange ratio was filed in Missouri; it was settled via a Confidential Settlement Agreement on June 24, 2020 and dismissed with prejudice two days later.
  - Two federal securities lawsuits (Dixon and Stein) alleging inadequate proxy disclosures were filed in the Southern District of New York; they were consolidated into a single class action on March 10, 2020.

- Overview: Note 19 outlines contingencies and legal proceedings affecting the Company, focusing on Brazilian tax matters, environmental remediation obligations, and U.S. shareholder litigation connected to the Amcor–Bemis merger.

- Brazil contingencies:
  - Ongoing governmental assessments and litigation primarily for excise and income taxes; Company expects to prevail on most matters and does not anticipate a material impact on results, financial position, or cash flows.
  - Potential need to post collateral in Brazilian courts; amounts pledged or potentially required are not expected to significantly impact liquidity.
  - Accruals recorded: $11.9 million at June 30, 2020 (vs. $16.4 million at June 30, 2019).
  - Estimated reasonably possible losses in excess of accruals: $18.4 million at June 30, 2020 (vs. $23.7 million at June 30, 2019).
  - Collateral posted as of June 30, 2020: $34.0 million in letters of credit, $0.9 million in judicial insurance, and $10.1 million in cash deposits.
  - Company continually evaluates likelihood and best estimates of loss; outcomes remain uncertain.

- Environmental matters:
  - Identified as a potentially responsible party at multiple U.S. waste sites; may face material remediation obligations. Insurance may only partly cover exposures.
  - Accruals recorded: $17.1 million for estimated future remediation at PRP sites.
  - Additional accruals: $46.6 million for remediation at various worldwide locations currently or formerly owned/operated by the Company.
  - Belief that accruals are adequate, though ultimate payments could exceed them; overall environmental obligations not expected to materially adversely affect liquidity, results, or financial condition.

- Legal proceedings related to Amcor–Bemis transaction:
  - Appraisal action by Burford Capital-funded shareholders:
    - Notice of intent (April 18, 2019), formal demand (June 24, 2019), petition filed (September 6, 2019), Bemis answer (November 4, 2019).
    - Resolved via Confidential Settlement Agreement on June 24, 2020; case dismissed with prejudice two days later.
  - Federal securities class action:
    - Two lawsuits (Dixon and Stein) filed April 15 and 17, 2019 in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York alleging inadequate proxy disclosures in violation of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and SEC rules.
    - Cases consolidated into a single class action on March 10, 2020.
text:
Contingencies - Brazil
        The Company's operations in Brazil are involved in various go vernmental assessments and litigation, principally related to cl aims for excise and income taxes. The Company will vigorously
defend its positions and believes it will prevail on most, if not all , of these matters. The Company does not believe that the ultimate resolution of these matters will materially impact the Company's
consolidated results of operations, financial position or cash flows. Under custo mary local regulations, the Company's Brazilian subsidiaries may n eed to post cash or other collateral if a challenge to
any administrative assessment proceeds to the Brazilian court sys tem; however, the level of cash or collateral already pledged or potentia lly required to be pledged would not significantly impact the
liquidity of Amcor. At June 30, 2020 and 2019, the Company has recorde d an accrual of $11.9 million and $16.4 million, respectively, includ ed in other non-current liabilities in the consolidated
balance sheet and has estimated a reasonably possible loss exp osure in excess of the accrual of $18.4 million and $23.7 million,  respectively. The litigation process is subject to many uncertaintie s
and the outcome of individual matters cannot be accurately predicte d. The Company routinely assesses these matters as to probability of ul timately incurring a liability and records the best estimate of
the ultimate loss in situations where the likelihood of an ultima te loss is probable. The Company's assessments are based on its kno wledge and experience, but the ultimate outcome of any of these
matters may differ from the Company's estimates.
        As of June 30, 2020, the Company provided letters of credit of $34.0 millio n, judicial insurance of $0.9 million and deposited cash of $10.1 mill ion with the courts to continue to defend the cases
referenced above.

title: Contingencies - Environmental Matters
heading: Contingencies - Environmental Matters
start_phrase: The Company, along with others, has been identified as a potentiall y responsible party ("PRP") at several waste disposal sites under U.S. federal and related state environmental statutes and regulations and may face potentially material environmental rem ediation obligations.
summary:
- Note 19 covers contingencies and legal proceedings affecting the company, with detail on Brazil tax matters, environmental obligations, and merger-related litigation.
- Brazil contingencies: Ongoing governmental assessments and litigation mainly for excise and income taxes; company plans vigorous defense and does not expect a material impact on results, financial position, or liquidity. Accruals recorded of $11.9 million (2020) and $16.4 million (2019) with additional reasonably possible losses of $18.4 million (2020) and $23.7 million (2019). Potential collateral requirements in Brazil are not expected to significantly affect liquidity; as of June 30, 2020, the company had $34.0 million in letters of credit, $0.9 million in judicial insurance, and $10.1 million in cash deposited with courts.
- Environmental matters: Identified as a potentially responsible party at several U.S. waste sites; insurance may only partially cover exposures. Accrued $17.1 million for estimated remediation at PRP sites and $46.6 million for remediation at various owned or formerly owned worldwide locations. Belief that accruals are adequate and obligations are not expected to be materially adverse, though ultimate costs could exceed accruals.
- Legal proceedings: 
  - Appraisal action by funds backed by Burford Capital related to the Amcor-Bemis transaction was settled on June 24, 2020 and dismissed with prejudice two days later.
  - Two federal securities lawsuits in the Southern District of New York alleging inadequate proxy disclosures about the Amcor-Bemis merger were consolidated into a single class action on March 10, 2020.
text:
Contingencies - Environmental Matters
        The Company, along with others, has been identified as a potentiall y responsible party ("PRP") at several waste disposal sites under U.S.  federal and related state environmental statutes and
regulations and may face potentially material environmental rem ediation obligations. While the Company benefits from various forms  of insurance policies, actual coverage may not, or only partially,
cover the total potential exposures. The Company has recorded $17.1 m illion aggregate accruals for its share of estimated future remediation c osts as these sites.
        In addition to the matters described above, the Company has also re corded aggregate accruals of $46.6 million for potential liabilities  for remediation obligations at various worldwide locations
that are owned or operated by the Company, or were formerly owned or operated.
        While the Company believes that its accruals are adequate t o cover its future obligations, there can be no assurance that the ultim ate payments will not exceed the accrued amounts. Nevertheless,
based on the available information, the Company does not believe that  its potential environmental obligations will have a material adve rse effect upon its liquidity, results of operations or financial
condition.

- The note outlines contingencies and legal proceedings as of June 30, 2020, focusing on Brazil tax matters, environmental obligations, and litigation related to the Amcor–Bemis merger.
- Brazil tax contingencies: Ongoing governmental assessments and litigation primarily for excise and income taxes. The company expects to prevail and does not anticipate a material impact on results, financial position, or cash flows. To continue defenses, the company provided $34.0 million in letters of credit, $0.9 million in judicial insurance, and deposited $10.1 million in cash; required collateral is not expected to significantly affect liquidity.

Recorded $17.1 million in accruals for PRP sites and $46.6 million for remediation at owned or formerly owned/operated locations worldwide. While accruals are believed adequate, ultimate costs could exceed them; obligations are not expected to materially affect liquidity, results, or financial condition.
- Legal proceedings: 
  - Appraisal action by Burford Capital–funded BCIM funds challenging the Amcor–Bemis exchange ratio was settled via a confidential agreement on June 24, 2020; case dismissed with prejudice two days later.
  - Two federal securities lawsuits (Dixon and Stein) alleging inadequate proxy disclosures in connection with the merger were filed in April 2019 and consolidated into a single class action on March 10, 2020 in the Southern District of New York.
  - A putative derivative suit in Missouri (Scarantino) alleges Bemis directors breached fiduciary duties and that Amcor aided and abetted. 
  - The company intends to defend these actions; potential damages cannot yet be reliably estimated and may be material if awarded.
text:
Legal Proceedings
        On April 18, 2019, prior to the closure of the Amcor and Bemis transaction , litigation funding firm, Burford Capital, notified Bemis on behalf of two shareholder funds (BCIM Strategic Value
Master Fund LP and BCIM SV SMA I LLC) that the funds would not accept the fixed e xchange ratio for Amcor shares and instead intended to file a case aski ng a Missouri state court to appraise the
value of their Bemis shares and compensate them accordingly. On June 24, 201 9, the Burford funds sent a formal written demand for payment of the fair value of the funds’ shares. On September 6,
2019, the Burford funds filed a Petition for Appraisal of Stock in the Missouri court. On  November 4, 2019, Bemis filed an Answer to the Petition for Appraisal of Stock. On June 24, 2020, the
parties entered into a Confidential Settlement Agreement and Release  of all claims and two days later the case was dismissed with prejud ice.
        Two lawsuits brought by purported holders of Bemis stock against Bem is and Bemis directors and officers are pending in federal court in the U .S. District Court for the Southern District of New
York, in which plaintiffs are seeking damages for alleged violations of t he Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, and U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission rules and regulations.
Plaintiffs allege a failure to disclose adequately information in the proxy statement issued in connection with the Amcor-Bemis merge r. The cases are: Dixon, et al. v. Bemis Company, Inc. et al.  and
Stein v. Bemis Company, Inc. et al ., which were instituted on April 15, 2019 and April 17, 2019, respectivel y. On March 10, 2020 the federal court in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District
of New York consolidated the two pending cases into a single clas s action.
102        In addition, a purported holder of Bemis stock filed a putative derivati ve suit in the Cole County Circuit Court, Nineteenth Judicial District of Missouri, against Bemis directors and Amcor,
alleging that the directors breached fiduciary duties in connection with  the Amcor-Bemis merger and that Amcor aided and abetted breaches of fidu ciary duty. The case is Scarantino, et al. v. Amcor
Limited, et al. , which was instituted on April 19, 2019.
        The Company intends to defend the claims made in the pending a ctions. It is too early for the Company to provide any reliable assessment  of the likely quantum of any damages that may
become payable if its defense is unsuccessful in whole or in part. Al though it is not possible at present to establish a reliable asses sment of damages, there can be no assurance that any damages that
may be awarded will not be material to the results of operations or fina ncial condition of the Company.

title: Segments
heading: Note 20 - Segments
start_phrase: The Company's business is organized and presented in the t wo reportable segments outlined below:
summary:
- Segment overview: The company reports two primary segments—Flexibles and Rigid Packaging—with “Other” capturing equity-method investments (including AMVIG), undistributed corporate costs, eliminations, and ancillary activities.
- Segment composition:
  - Flexibles: Flexible and film packaging for food & beverage, medical/pharma, fresh produce, snacks, personal care, and other industries.
  - Rigid Packaging: Rigid plastic containers and plastic caps serving beverages (CSDs, water, juices, sports drinks, dairy, spirits, beer) and food/personal care.
- Segment structure changes post-Bemis acquisition: In FY20, Flexibles Americas was split into Flexibles North America and Flexibles Latin America; five Flexibles operating segments were aggregated into one reporting segment based on similarity of economics, products, technologies, customers, delivery models, and regulation.
- Performance measure change: Beginning Q4 FY19 (in connection with the Bemis acquisition), management shifted segment performance metric to Adjusted EBIT from continuing operations. Adjusted EBIT is operating income adjusted for specified non-core items and includes equity in income (loss) of affiliates.
- Governance: The Global Management Team (GMT)—the CEO and direct reports—allocates resources and evaluates performance using Adjusted EBIT; segment accounting policies align with Note 2.
- AMVIG treatment: Accounted for under the equity method; its results are excluded from segment net sales.
- FY20–FY18 summary financials by segment:
  - Net sales grew to $12.5B in FY20 (from $9.5B in FY19), with Flexibles as the primary contributor; intersegment sales were minimal.
  - Adjusted EBIT in FY20: $1,497.1M (Flexibles $1,335.1M; Rigid Packaging $290.1M; Other $(128.1)M).
- Reconciliation items from Adjusted EBIT to EBIT include: restructuring programs, impairments in equity-method investments (AMVIG), material acquisition and integration costs (notably Bemis), amortization of acquired intangibles (including sales backlog), economic net investment hedging impacts, hyperinflation effects (Argentina), net legal settlements, and pension settlements.
- FY20 EBIT from continuing operations: $995.9M; interest income/expense and equity in income (loss) of affiliates disclosed; pre-tax income provided.
- Capital expenditures and D&A: FY20 capex $399.5M; depreciation and amortization $607.2M, both detailed by segment.
- Assets: Total assets by segment are not disclosed as GMT does not use them for performance/resource allocation.
- Customer concentration: No single customer >10% of sales in FY20; PepsiCo accounted for ~11% in FY19 and FY18 across both segments; no other customer exceeded 10% in those years.
- Product sales mix: FY20 comprised Films and other flexible products ($8.64B), Specialty flexible folding cartons ($1.11B), and Containers, preforms and closures ($2.72B).
- Geographic details:
  - Net sales disaggregated by region (North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia Pacific) for FY18–FY20, by segment; Jersey (domicile) had no sales.
  - Long-lived assets totaled $3.61B at June 30, 2020, with $1.56B in the U.S. and the remainder in other countries; none in Jersey and no single other country >10%.
- Note 21 – Deed of Cross Guarantee: Amcor plc and specified wholly owned Australian subsidiaries entered a Deed of Cross Guarantee (June 24, 2019), with ARP North America Holdco Ltd and ARP LATAM Holdco Ltd added on Sept. 25, 2019; subsidiaries are relieved from preparing separate financial and directors’ reports under ASIC Instrument 2016/785; ASIC-required consolidated financial statements for the deed group will be presented.
text:
Note 20 - Segments
        The Company's business is organized and presented in the t wo reportable segments outlined below:
Flexibles:  Consists of operations that manufacture flexible and film packaging in  the food and beverage, medical and pharmaceutical, fresh produce, snack food , personal care, and other industries.
Rigid Packaging:  Consists of operations that manufacture rigid plastic containers for a b road range of predominantly beverage and food products, including carbonated soft drinks, water, juices,
sports drinks, milk-based beverages, spirits and beer, sauces, dressi ngs, spreads and personal care items and plastic caps for a wide variety of a pplications.
        Other consists of the Company's equity method investments, incl uding AMVIG, undistributed corporate expenses, intercompany eliminati ons and other business activities.
        Operating segments are organized along the Company's product lin es and geographical areas. In conjunction with the acquisition of Be mis, the Company reassessed its segment reporting
structure in the first fiscal quarter of 2020 and elected to disaggregate  the Flexibles Americas operating segment into Flexibles North Am erica and Flexibles Latin America. The five Flexibles
operating segments (Flexibles Europe, Middle East and Africa; Flexibles North  America, Flexibles Latin America; Flexibles Asia Pacific and S pecialty Cartons) have been aggregated in the Flexibles
reporting segment as they exhibit similarity in economic characte ristics and future prospects, similarity in the products they offer, t heir production technologies, the customers they serve, the nature of
their service delivery models, and their regulatory environments.
        In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2019, in connection with the acquisi tion of Bemis, the Company changed its measure of segment performance from adjusted operating income to adjusted
earnings before interest and tax ("Adjusted EBIT") from continuing operation s. The Company's chief operating decision maker, the Global Manage ment Team ("GMT"), evaluates performance and
allocates resources based on Adjusted EBIT from continuing operations.  The Company defines Adjusted EBIT as operating income adjusted to e liminate the impact of certain items that the Company
does not consider indicative of its ongoing operating performance and to include equity in income (loss) of affiliated companies. The GMT cons ists of the Managing Director and Chief Executive
Officer and his direct reports and provides strategic direction and mana gement oversight of the day to day activities of the Company.
        The accounting policies of the reportable segments are the same  as those in the consolidated financial statements and are disc ussed in Note 2, "Significant Accounting Policies." The Company
also has investments in operations in AMVIG that are accounted for under the equity method of accounting and, accordingly, those results are n ot included in segment net sales.

title: Deed of Cross Guarantee
heading: Note 21 - Deed of Cross Guarantee
start_phrase: The parent entity, Amcor plc, and its wholly owned subsidiaries listed below are subject to a Deed of Cross Guarantee dated June 24, 2019 (the "Deed") under which each company guarantees the debts of the others:
summary:
- Note 21 outlines a Deed of Cross Guarantee dated June 24, 2019 under which Amcor plc and specified wholly owned subsidiaries guarantee each other’s debts. The closed (and extended closed) group as of June 30, 2020 includes multiple Australian entities plus ARP North America Holdco Ltd and ARP LATAM Holdco Ltd (both added September 25, 2019). No other additions, removals, or disposals since inception.
- By joining the Deed, these subsidiaries are relieved from preparing separate financial and directors’ reports under ASIC Corporations (Wholly‑owned Companies) Instrument 2016/785. ASIC‑specific consolidated financial disclosures for the deed group are provided.
- Statement of Income (in millions): FY2020 vs FY2019 shows net sales 323.6 vs 352.8; significant other income driving operating income 4,192.0 vs 1,025.7; net income 4,163.8 vs 995.3; 2020 includes an income tax credit.
- Summarized Statement of Comprehensive Income: OCI of 32.2 in 2020 vs 65.4 in 2019 (cash flow hedges, FX translation, net investment hedges); total comprehensive income 4,196.0 vs 1,060.7.
- Summarized Statement of Income and Accumulated Losses: retained earnings rose from 2,519.0 to 5,935.2 in 2020 after net income and dividends; dividends recognized 747.6 (2020) and 665.9 (2019).
- Balance Sheet (in millions): total assets 13,551.9 (2020) vs 11,589.0 (2019), driven by other non‑current assets; liabilities decreased to 1,067.8 from 2,022.8 with lower long‑term debt (355.8 vs 1,587.7) but higher short‑term debt (507.3 vs 155.3); shareholders’ equity increased to 12,484.1 from 9,566.2.
- Note 22 provides supplemental cash flow details: interest paid (net) 212.3 (2020), 219.8 (2019), 209.4 (2018); income taxes paid 304.4 (2020), 147.7 (2019), 149.7 (2018); non‑cash investing includes accrued but unpaid PP&E purchases of 78.0, 75.0, and 68.4; non‑cash financing includes 2019 equity issuance of 5,229.6 for the Bemis acquisition.

title: Controls and Procedures
heading: Item 9A. Controls and Procedures
start_phrase: Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Of ficer and Chief Financial Officer, has evaluated the effectiveness of o ur disclosure controls and procedures as of June 30, 2020.
summary:
- Item 9: Reports no changes in, or disagreements with, accountants on accounting or financial disclosure.
- Item 9A: Management evaluated disclosure controls as of June 30, 2020 and concluded they were not effective due to a continuing material weakness in internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) related to segregation of duties within key IT systems used for period-end reporting. No misstatements occurred, but the deficiency could have led to them. ICFR is assessed under the COSO 2013 framework and was audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers AG.
- Remediation plan: Implement new security roles, automate segregation-of-duties monitoring, add compensating controls, and provide training; rollout focused on largest standardized ERP locations in FY2020 with expansion in FY2021. Remediation expected by end of FY2021, though COVID-19 may delay timing.
- Completed remediation: A separate material weakness related to U.S. GAAP technical accounting and U.S. registrant filing experience has been remediated through added staffing, policy alignment, enhanced close reviews, and training; tested and deemed effective by Q4 FY2020.
- Changes in ICFR: Aside from the actions described, no changes in Q4 FY2020 that materially affected or are likely to materially affect ICFR.
- Item 9B: No other information.
