title: Termination for Cause or Violation of Non-Compete Restrictions
heading: 5.2 Termination for Cause or Violation of Non-Compete Restrictions
start_phrase: Notwithstanding any provisions in the Plan to the contrary, any Participant terminated for cause shall forfeit 100% of the Participant’s Accounts.
summary:
- Termination for cause results in forfeiture of 100% of a Participant’s Accounts. “Cause” includes fraud, misappropriation or embezzlement of Employer assets, and intentional, material damage to Employer or Affiliate property, as determined in the Committee’s sole discretion.
- Violation of non‑compete restrictions (working for, advising, or assisting a “competing business” before or after a 409A-defined separation from service, including death) results in forfeiture of 100% of Employer Contributions. If a partial distribution was already made, any unpaid portion is forfeited. A “competing business” is any entity conducting the same or competing business as the Company, as determined by the Committee.
- Forfeitures are used to reduce Employer Contributions for the current or future Plan Years, or to pay reasonable Plan administrative expenses.
- Allocation of contributions (Salary Deferral, Bonus, Employer Make-Up Matching, Employer Make-Up Pension, Employer Special, and Employer 10% Target Contributions) to Participants’ Accounts occurs periodically as determined by the Committee.

Beginning in 2007, the Plan uses class-year accounting with separate subaccounts within 409A Accounts. Accounts are credited with earnings, losses, distributions, and contributions as of accounting dates set by the Investment Committee. All credited amounts are for bookkeeping only and remain Employer assets subject to the claims of the Employer’s general creditors.

In addition, any Participant who works for, counsels, advises, or otherwise assists a person, entity or business that is a “competing business,” before or after the Participant’s separation from service (within the meaning of Section 409A of the Code and the regulations, notices and other guidance thereunder, including death) from an Employer, shall forfeit 100% o f the Participant’s Employer Contributions. text: A Particip ant may elect the timing and form of payment for the Participant’s Grandfathered Accounts by completing a benefit election form prescribed by the Committee. A Participant may elect to receive the Participant’s Grandfathered Accounts as of: (i) the Participant’s termination of employment, or  (ii) a specified date elected by the Participant. If a Participant terminates service from all Employers and their Affiliates prior to retirement, the Participant will receive a distribution of the Participant’s Grandfathered Account in a lump sum. If a Participant requests a distribution prior to service termination, or if a Participant terminates service due to retirement or Disability, a Participant’s Grandfathered Account may be distributed in: (i) a lump sum, or (ii) substantially equal annual installments payable at the Participant’s election over a one-year to ten-year period specified by the Participant. The benefit election form will be valid as to all amounts in a Participant’s Grandfathered Accounts unless the Participant alters the Participant’s benefit election form, provided that a Participant must submit a revised benefit election form at least 12 months prior to a distribution. If a Participant fails to make a selection among the available forms of payment, the Participant shall receive payment in a lump sum. The Committee shall determine if a Participant’s termination is due to retirement or Disability. 7.2

title: Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts
heading: 7.2 Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts
start_phrase: Prior to the a llocation of Employee Contributions to the Participant’s 409A Accounts, a Participant must elect the timing and form of payment for such Employee Contributions from the Participant’s 409A Accoun ts by completing a distribution election form in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Committee (the “Initial Election”).
summary:
- Section 7 outlines when and how benefits are paid under the plan, with separate rules for Grandfathered Accounts and 409A Accounts (Employee and Employer Contributions), and compliance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code.

- 7.1 Grandfathered Accounts:
  - Participants elect timing (at termination of employment or a specified date) and form (lump sum or 1–10 years of substantially equal annual installments in certain cases) via a Committee-prescribed form.
  - If service ends before retirement, payment is a mandatory lump sum.
  - If requesting distribution before termination, or if termination is due to retirement or Disability, payment may be lump sum or installments over 1–10 years.
  - Elections apply to all Grandfathered amounts unless changed; any change must be submitted at least 12 months before the distribution.
  - Default if no election: lump sum.
  - The Committee determines whether a termination qualifies as retirement or Disability.

- 7.2 Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts:
  - Before contributions are allocated, Participants must make an Initial Election for timing and form; beginning with 2007, a separate election is required for each year’s Employee Contributions.
  - Distribution timing may be the earlier of: (i) the first day of the 7th month after separation from service (as defined under 409A, including death), or (ii) a Participant-elected specific date.
  - Form of payment: lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years; installment series is treated as a single payment under 409A regulations.
  - Initial Election governs pre-2007 Employee Contributions (and earnings/losses) unless replaced by a Second Election, which:
    - Takes effect 12 months after it is made.
    - Must defer payment at least 5 years beyond the original payment date.
    - Must be made at least 12 months before the first scheduled payment.
    - Cannot accelerate payments and can only choose among permitted forms.
  - No Second Election is allowed for Employee Contributions made on or after January 1, 2007.
  - Default if no election: lump sum on the first day of the 7th month following separation.
  - Beginning January 1, 2007, elections for 2005–2006 Employee Contributions may be modified, subject to the Second Election restrictions.

- 7.3 Employer Contributions in 409A Accounts:
  - Upon selection to receive Employer Contributions, Participants elect the form of payment via a Committee-prescribed distribution election; starting with 2007, a separate election is required for each year’s Employer Contributions.
  - Employer Contributions are distributed on the first day of the 13th month following separation from service (as defined under 409A, including death).

- Outlines “Second Election” restrictions for Employee Contributions: 12-month waiting period to take effect, at least a 5-year deferral beyond the prior payment date, must be made at least 12 months before the first scheduled payment, no acceleration allowed, and limited to approved payment forms; no Second Elections allowed for Employee Contributions made on or after January 1, 2007.

- Sets rules for Employer Contributions in 409A Accounts: participants elect payment form; beginning with 2007 contributions, a separate election is required each year; distributions occur on the first day of the thirteenth month after separation (including death).
- Specifies allowable forms for Employer Contributions: lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years; installments are treated as a single payment under 409A; once elected, neither timing nor form may be changed; default is lump sum if no election is made.
- Establishes hardship distribution provisions: available from vested accounts upon an Unforeseeable Financial Emergency; paid in a lump sum within 90 days; paid from 409A Accounts before Grandfathered Accounts.
- Defines Unforeseeable Financial Emergency (illness/accident of participant or dependent, casualty loss, or similar extraordinary, unforeseeable events beyond the participant’s control), requires reduction for insurance/reimbursement and feasible asset liquidation, and leaves eligibility/amount determinations to the Committee based on facts and circumstances.
- States that receiving a hardship distribution suspends the participant’s Employee Contributions for the remainder of that calendar year.
text:
Employer Contributions in 409A Accounts Upon being selected by the Committe e to receive Employer Contributions, a Participant will elect the form of payment for theParticipant’s Employer Contributions held in the Participant’s 409A Accounts by completing a distribution election form in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Committee. Beginning with 20 07 contributions, a Participant shall make a separate distribution election form for each year of Employer Contributions. A Participant’s Employer Contributions held in the Participant’s 409A  Accounts shall be distributed upon the first day of the thirteenth month following Participant’s separation from service (within the meaning of Section 409A of the Code and the regulations, notices and other guidance thereunder, including death) from the Employer. The Employer Contri butions in a Participant’s 409A Accounts may be distributed in: -17- 
(i) a lump sum, or (ii) substantially equal annual installments payable at the Participant’s election over a two-year to ten-year period specified by the Participant. For purposes of the Plan, a series of installment payments shall be treated as a single payment in accordance with the regulations under Section 409A of the Code. Once such election is made, neither the Participant nor the Employe r may change the timing or form of distribution of a Participant’s Employer Contribution s held in the Participant’s 409A Accounts. If a Participant fails to make a payment election, the Participant shall receive payment of Employer Contributions in a lump sum. 7.4

title: Hardship Distributions
heading: 7.4 Hardship Distributio ns
start_phrase: A Participant may receive a distribution from the Participant’s vested Accounts for hardship reasons, provided the Participant has suffered an Unforeseeable Financial Emergency (as defined below ).
summary:
- Describes distribution options for Employer Contributions in 409A Accounts: either a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years, at the participant’s election.
- States that an installment series is treated as a single payment under Section 409A regulations.
- Once a payment election is made, neither the participant nor the employer may change the timing or form of distribution; absent an election, payment defaults to a lump sum.
- Outlines hardship distribution rules: available in case of an “Unforeseeable Financial Emergency,” paid in a lump sum within 90 days of request.
- Establishes payment ordering for hardship withdrawals: amounts are taken from 409A Accounts before Grandfathered Accounts.
- Defines “Unforeseeable Financial Emergency” as severe financial hardship arising from sudden illness/accident of the participant or dependent, loss of property due to casualty, or similar extraordinary, unforeseeable events beyond the participant’s control.
- Requires that hardship distribution amounts be reduced by insurance/reimbursements or by liquidation of assets, unless liquidation would itself cause severe hardship.
- Assigns the plan committee authority to determine eligibility and payment amounts based on all relevant facts and circumstances.
- Provides that receiving a hardship distribution suspends the participant’s employee contributions for the remainder of the calendar year.
text:
A Participant may receive a distribution from the Participant’s vested Accounts for hardship reasons, provided the Participant has suffered an Unforeseeable Financial Emergency (as defined below ). The Committee may request such evidence of a hardship as it deems necessary. All hardship distributions will be made in a lump sum within 90 days following the Participant’s hardship request; provided, however, that hardship distributions shall be paid from 409A Accounts prior to payment from  Grandfathered Accounts. The following rules shall apply to a hardship distribution: (a) An “Unforeseeable Financial Emergency” is a severe financial hardship to the Participant resulting from: (i) a sudden and unexpected illness or accident of the Participant or of a dependent of the Participant, (ii) loss of the Participant’s property due to casualty, or (iii) such other similar extraordinary and unforeseeable circumstances arising as a result of events beyond the control of the Participan t. (b) The amount of hardship distribution on behalf of an Unforeseeable Financial Emergency will b e reduced to the extent that it is or may be relieved: (i) through reimbursement or compensation by  insurance or otherwise, or (ii) by liquidation of the Participant’s assets, to the extent the liquidation of such assets wouldnot itself cause severe financial hardship. (c) The determination of whether a Participant has suffered an Unforeseeable Financial Emergency, and the amount of payment to which the Participant is entitled, shall be determined by the Committee based on all of the relevant facts and circumstances. If a Participant receives a hardship distribution from the Plan, then the Participant’s Employee Contributions shall be suspended for the remainder of the calendar year in which such distribution occurred. -18-

title: Payments After Death
heading: 7.5 Payments After Death
start_phrase: If a Participant dies before receiving the entire balance of the Participant’s Accounts, the remaining balance in the Participant’s Accounts shall become 100% vested and shall be paid to the Participant’s Beneficiaries designated in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Committee.
summary:
- Payments after death (Section 7.5): If a participant dies before full distribution, all account balances become 100% vested and are paid to designated beneficiaries in a single lump sum within 90 days after the Committee is notified of the death.
- Payments upon disability (Section 7.6): Regardless of prior elections, any accounts not yet in distribution are automatically distributed as soon as administratively practicable after a Disability (as defined in 2.10).
  - Grandfathered Accounts: payable either as a lump sum or in substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years, per the participant’s election; changes to disability distribution elections must comply with subsection 7.1.
  - 409A Accounts: distributed according to the participant’s elections applicable to each year of contributions; changes to disability distribution elections for Employee Contributions must comply with subsection 7.2.
- Special distribution rules for 409A Accounts (Section 7.7):
  - If Code Section 162(m) would limit or eliminate the employer’s deduction, payment is deferred to the first year the deduction is expected to be available or to the year of separation from employment.
  - If payment would violate securities or other laws, or breach loan covenants/contract terms causing material harm, payment is deferred to the first calendar year when no such violation or material harm is anticipated.
  - Mentions plan payments related to employment taxes or income inclusion (text truncated).

Payment of the remaining balance of the Participant’s Accounts shall be made in a s ingle lump sum within 90 days following the date on which the Committee is notified of the Participant’s death. 7.6

title: Payments Upon Disability
heading: 7.6 Payments Upon Disability
start_phrase: Notwithstanding a Participant’s elections and any provisio n of the Plan to the contrary, all Accounts that have not yet commenced distribution shall automatically be distributed to a Participant as soon as administratively practicable following the Participant’s Disability as defined under subsection 2.10.
summary:
- Payment after death: If a participant dies before full distribution, the remaining account balance becomes 100% vested and is paid to designated beneficiaries in a single lump sum within 90 days after the Committee is notified.
- Payment upon disability: Upon a disability (as defined in the plan), any accounts not already in distribution are automatically distributed as soon as administratively practicable.
  - Grandfathered Accounts: Paid either as a lump sum or in substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years per the participant’s election; any changes to disability-related elections must follow the plan’s change rules in subsection 7.1.
  - 409A Accounts: Distributed according to the participant’s prior distribution elections for each contribution year; changes to disability-related elections for Employee Contributions must comply with subsection 7.2.
- Special distribution rules for 409A Accounts:
  - Section 162(m) limitation: If payment would not be deductible due to the corporate tax deduction limit, payment is deferred to the first year it is expected to be deductible or to the year of separation from employment.
  - Legal/contractual constraints: If payment would violate securities or other laws, or breach loan covenants/contract terms causing material harm, payment is deferred to the first year such issues no longer apply and payment would not cause material harm.
  - Notes an allowance for payments related to employment taxes or income inclusion (text truncated).
text: Payments Upon Disability Notwithstanding a Participant’s elections and any provisio n of the Plan to the contrary, all Accounts that have not yet commenced distribution shall automatically be distributed to a Participant as soon as administratively practicable following the Participant’s Disability as defined under subsection 2.10. Upon Disability, a Participant will receive distribution of the Participant’s Grandfathered Accounts either in: (i) a lump sum; or (ii) substantially equal annual installments payable at the Participant’s election over a two-year to ten-year period specified by the Participant. If a Participant wishes to make changes to any Disability distribution election form with respect to the Participant’s Grandfathered Accounts, such changes must comply with the rules contained in subsection 7.1. Upon a Participant’s Disability, the Participant’s 409A Accounts shall be distributed to the Participant in accordance with the forms of payment elected on the Participant’s distribution election form applicable to each year of contributions. If a Participant wishes to make changes to any Disability distribution election form with respect to the Employee Contributions in the Participant’s 409A Accounts, such changes must comply with the rules contain ed in subsection 7.2. 7.7

title: Special Distribution Rules for 409A Accounts
heading: 7.7 Special Distribution Rules for 409A Accounts
start_phrase: If the Company or Affiliate’ s deduction for payment of all or any portion of to a Participant’s 409A Accounts would be limited oreliminated by the application of Section 162(m) of the Code, then the Plan will defer payment of such Participant’s 409A Accounts either (i) to a date in the first year in which the Company or the Com mittee reasonably anticipates that such payment will not result in a deduction limitation under Section 162(m) or (ii) to the year in which the Participant’s separation from employment occurs.
summary:
- Payments after death: If a participant dies before full distribution, all account balances become 100% vested and are paid in a single lump sum to designated beneficiaries within 90 days of the Committee being notified.
- Payments upon disability: All undistributed accounts are paid as soon as administratively practicable after the participant’s Disability (as defined in 2.10). Grandfathered Accounts are paid either as a lump sum or in substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years per the participant’s election (changes must follow 7.1). 409A Accounts are paid per the participant’s prior elections for each contribution year (changes to Employee Contributions must follow 7.2).
- Special rules for 409A Accounts: Payments are deferred if they would be nondeductible under Section 162(m), until the first year the deduction is expected to be allowed or the year of separation from employment. Payments are also deferred if they would violate securities/applicable laws or loan/contract terms causing material harm, until the first year no such violation/harm is anticipated. The Plan may make payments to cover employment taxes (FICA and related income tax) or due to 409A income inclusion, consistent with Treasury Regulations and IRS guidance. If a payment window spans two Plan Years, the recipient cannot choose the tax year of payment.
- Beneficiary designations: Participants may designate primary and contingent beneficiaries (including trusts/estates) and allocation proportions for all accounts, and may change designations; the last filed designation controls. If none is on file, balances are paid to the participant’s estate.
- Facility of payment: If a recipient is under a legal disability or unable to manage affairs, payments may be made to a legal representative or applied for the person’s benefit as determined by the Committee.
- Unclaimed benefits: If a participant/beneficiary’s whereabouts are unknown and benefits are unclaimed within two years after employment termination, the Committee may pay as if the participant died. If neither the participant nor any beneficiary can be located within three years after termination, all benefits are irrevocably forfeited.

Special Distribution Rules for 409A Accounts If the Company or Affiliate’ s deduction for payment of all or any portion of to a Participant’s 409A Accounts would be limited oreliminated by the application of Section 162(m) of the Code, then the Plan will defer payment of such Participant’s 409A Accounts either (i) to a date in the first year in which the Company or the Com mittee reasonably anticipates that such payment will not result in a deduction limitation under Section 162(m) or (ii) to the year in which the Participant’s separation from employment occurs. If payment of all or any portion of the Participant’s 409A Accounts would violate securities or other applicable laws, or would violate loan covenants or other contractual terms to which the Company or an Affiliate is a party and such violation would result in material harm to the Company or an Affiliate, then payment of the Participant’s 409A Accounts will be made in the first calendar year: (i) in which the Company or Committee reasonably anticipates that the payment would not violate loan or other similar contractual terms and would not result in material harm to the Company or an Affiliate, and (ii) in which the payment would not result in a violation of securities or other applicable laws. Plan payments intended to pay employment taxes, or made as a result of income inclusion of an amount of a Participant’s -19- 
benefit as a result of a failure to satisfy Section 409A of the Code, shall be permitted at the Company or Committee’s discretion at any time to the extent provided in Treasury Regulations under Section 409A of the Code and IRS Notice 2005-1, Q&A-15, and any applicable subsequent gu idance. “Employment taxes” shall include the Federal Income Contributions Act (FICA) tax imposed  under Sections 3101 and 3121(v)(2) of the Code on compensation deferred under the  Plan (the “FICA Amount”), the income tax imposed under Section 3401 of the Code on the FICA Am ount, and any amounts utilized to pay the additional income tax under Section 3401 of the Code a ttributable to the pyramiding Section 3401 wages and taxes. If any applicable payment period begins in one Plan Year and ends in the following Plan Year, the Participant or the Participant’s Beneficiary (as the case may be) shall not have the right to designate the year of the payment. 7.8

title: Designation of Beneficiary
heading: 7.8 Designation of Beneficiary
start_phrase: A Participant may, by completing a Beneficiary designation form in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Committee, designate one or more primary and contingent Beneficiaries (which may include a trust or an estate) to receive the Participant’s Account balance following the Participant’s death and may designate the proportions in which such Beneficiaries receive payments.
summary:
- 409A compliance/corrections: The Company/Committee may take actions permitted under Treasury Regulations, IRS Notice 2005-1 Q&A-15, and subsequent guidance to address failures under Section 409A.
- Employment taxes defined: Includes FICA on deferred compensation (Sections 3101 and 3121(v)(2)), income tax under Section 3401 on the FICA amount, and additional income tax attributable to pyramiding wages and taxes.
- Payment timing: If a payment period spans two Plan Years, the Participant/Beneficiary cannot choose the tax year of payment.
- Beneficiary designations: Participants may designate primary and contingent beneficiaries (including trusts/estates), specify proportions, and change designations; the last on file controls. If none is on file, the estate receives the balance.
- Facility of payment: If a payee is under legal disability or unable to manage affairs, payments may be made to a legal representative or applied for the person’s benefit as the Committee decides.
- Unclaimed benefits: If whereabouts are unknown and benefits are unclaimed within two years after employment termination, the Committee may pay as if the Participant had died. If the Participant/Beneficiaries cannot be located within three years after termination, all benefits are irrevocably forfeited.
text: Designation of Beneficiary A Participant may, by completing a Beneficiary designation form in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Committee, designate one or more primary and contingent Beneficiaries (which may include a trust or an estate) to receive the Participant’s Account balance following the Participant’s death and may designate the proportions in which such Beneficiaries receive payments. A Participant’s Beneficiary designation shall apply to all of his Accounts under the Plan. A Participant may change such designations from time to time, and the last designation filed prior to the Participant’s death shall control. If no Beneficiary designation form was filed by the Participant prior to the Participant’s death, the Participant’s remaining Account balance will be paid to the Participant’s estate. 7.9

title: Facility of Payment
heading: 7.9 Facility of Payment
start_phrase: Any amounts payable under the Plan to a Participant or Beneficiary who is under a legal disability or who, in the judgment of the Committee, is unable to manage such person’saffairs, may be paid to the legal representative of such person or may be applied for the benefit of such person in any manner the Committee shall select.
summary:
- Compliance with Section 409A: Allows Company/Committee discretion to accelerate or adjust payments only as permitted by Treasury Regulations and IRS Notice 2005-1 (Q&A-15) and later guidance. Defines “Employment taxes” to include FICA on deferred compensation (Sections 3101 and 3121(v)(2)), income tax under Section 3401 on the FICA Amount, and amounts to cover pyramiding wages/taxes. If a payment period spans two Plan Years, the recipient cannot choose the tax year of payment.
- Beneficiary Designation (Section 7.8): Participants may designate primary and contingent beneficiaries (including trusts/estates) for all Plan accounts, specify proportions, and update designations; the last filed designation controls. If none is on file at death, benefits go to the estate.
- Facility of Payment (Section 7.9): If a payee is under a legal disability or unable to manage affairs, payments may be made to a legal representative or applied for the person’s benefit as the Committee decides.
- Unclaimed Benefits (Section 7.10): If a participant/beneficiary cannot be located and no claim is made within two years after employment termination, the Committee may pay benefits as if the participant had died. If neither the participant nor any beneficiary can be located within three years after termination, all vested benefits are irrevocably forfeited.

title: Unclaimed Benefits
heading: 7.10 Unclaimed Benefits
start_phrase: If a Participant or Beneficiary’s whereabouts are unknown to the Employer, and if the Participant or the Participant’s Beneficiary fails to claim the Participant’s benefits within two years following termination of the Participant’s employment, the Committee may elect to make payment of the Participant or Beneficiary’s vested benefits as if they had died.
summary:
- Clarifies Section 409A compliance: the Company/Committee may make distributions or take actions permitted under Treasury Regulations and IRS Notice 2005-1 (and subsequent guidance), including to address failures under Section 409A.
- Defines “Employment taxes” to include FICA on deferred compensation under Code Sections 3101 and 3121(v)(2), income tax under Section 3401 on the FICA amount, and additional amounts to cover pyramiding wages and taxes.
- Specifies that when a payment period spans two Plan Years, the Participant/Beneficiary cannot choose the tax year of payment.
- Outlines beneficiary designations: Participants may designate primary/contingent beneficiaries (including trusts/estates) and allocation proportions; the latest designation controls; if none, payment defaults to the estate.
- Provides for payment to or for the benefit of individuals under legal disability or unable to manage affairs, at the Committee’s discretion.
- Addresses unclaimed benefits: if benefits are unclaimed within two years after employment termination and the individual’s whereabouts are unknown, payments may be made as if the Participant had died; if neither the Participant nor any Beneficiary can be located within three years after termination, all benefits are irrevocably forfeited.
text: Unclaimed Benefits If a Participant or Beneficiary’s whereabouts are unknown to the Employer, and if the Participant or the Participant’s Beneficiary fails to claim the Participant’s benefits within two years following termination of the Participant’s employment, the Committee may elect to make payment of the Participant or Beneficiary’s vested benefits as if they had died. If the Employer is unable to locate the Participant or any Beneficiary within three years following the Participant’s employment termination, the Participant and all of the Participant’s designated Beneficiaries shall forfeit all benefits irrevocably. -20-

title: Nature of Interest of Participant
heading: SECTION 8 Nature of Interest of Participant
start_phrase: Participation in this Plan will not create, in favor of any Participant, any right or lien in or against any of the assets of any Employer, and a Participant’s Account balances shall remain an unrestricted asset of the Participant’s Employer.
summary:
- Participants have no lien or right against employer assets; account balances remain employer assets.
- Benefits are non-assignable and cannot be anticipated, pledged, transferred, or encumbered.
- All benefits are paid in cash from the employer’s general funds; no separate fund or asset segregation is created.
- The Plan does not create a trust or fiduciary relationship; the employer’s promise to pay remains unfunded with respect to participants.
- Administration is by a Committee with authority to interpret the Plan, resolve ambiguities, adopt rules, enforce the Plan and any trust, direct trustees on distributions, provide employers with required information, and hire/delegate to service providers in writing.
- An Investment Committee has full authority over appointing trustees and investment managers and overseeing investment of Plan assets.
- Employers may withhold required federal, state, or local taxes from Plan payments.
text: SECTION 8 Nature of Interest of Participant Participation in this Plan will not create, in favor of any Participant, any right or lien in or against any of the assets of any Employer, and a Participant’s Account balances shall remain an unrestricted asset of the Participant’s Employer. A Participant’s rights to benefits payable under the Plan are not subject in any manner to anticipation, alienation, sale, transfer, assignment, pledge, or encumbrance. All payments hereunder shall be paid in cash from the general funds of the applicable Employer and no special or separate fund shall be established and no other segregation of assets shall be made to assure the payment of benefits hereunder. Nothing contained in this Plan, and no action taken pursuant to its provisions, shall create or be con strued to create a trust of any kind, or a fiduciary relationship, between any Employer and a Participant or any other person, and each Employer’s promise to pay benefits hereunder shall at all times remain unfunded as to the Participant. -21-

title: Committee
heading: 9.1 Committee
start_phrase: This Plan will be administered by the Committee.
summary:
- Establishes that the Plan is administered by a Committee.
- Grants the Committee broad, discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, resolve ambiguities, adopt administrative rules, and enforce the Plan and Trust.

- Permits the Committee to hire and delegate duties to agents (e.g., attorneys, accountants, actuaries), including individuals also employed by the Employers, with all delegations and acceptances in writing.
- Assigns the Investment Committee full authority over appointing trustees and investment managers and overseeing investment of Plan assets.
- Confirms Employers’ right to withhold required federal, state, and local taxes from Plan payments.

text: Powers of the Administrative and Investment Committees The Committee’s powers will include, but will not be limited to, the power: (a) to interpret, in its sole discretion, the terms and provisions of the Plan and to determine any and all questions arising under the Plan, including without limitation, the right to remedy possible ambiguities, inconsistencies, or omissions by a general rule or particular decision, (b) to adopt such rules of procedure and regulations as in its opinion may be  necessary for the proper and efficient administration of the Plan and as are consistent with the Plan and Trust agreement, (c) to enforce the Plan in accordance with the terms of the Plan and the Trust and in accordance with the rules and regulations the Committee has adopted, (d) to direct the Trustees as respects payments or distributions from the Trust in accordance with the provisions of the Plan, (e) to furnish the Employers with such information as may be required by them for tax or other purposes in connection with the Plan, and (f) to employ agents, attorneys, accountants, actuaries or other persons (who also may be employed by the Employers) and to allocate or delegate to them such powers, rights and duties as the Committee may consider necessary or advisable to properly carry out administration of the Plan, provided that such allocation or delegation and the acceptance thereof by such agents, attorneys, accountants, actuaries or other persons, shall be in writing. The Investment Committee’s powers will include, but will not be limited to, the power to exercise full authority and control with respect to the appointment of trustees and investment managers and the investment of Plan assets generally. 9.3

title: Retirement Claims Procedures
heading: 9.4 Retirement Claims Procedures
start_phrase: To the extent that a Participant’s claim relates to a determination with respect to his Accounts, other than a Disability determination, the Committee will provide the Participant with notice of the status of his claim for retirement benefits within a reasonable period of time after a complete claim has been filed, but no later than 90 days after receipt of the Participant’s benefit claim.
summary:
- Scope: Outlines Retirement Claims Procedures for benefit claims related to a participant’s accounts other than disability determinations, and begins the Disability Claims Procedures section.
- Initial claim decision (retirement claims):
  - Committee must issue a status/decision within a reasonable time, no later than 90 days after receiving a complete claim.
  - One 90-day extension permitted for special circumstances with notice given before the initial 90-day period ends.
- Incomplete claims:
  - Participant is notified of missing information and given 90 days to supply it.
  - The Committee’s response deadline is tolled from the notice of insufficiency until the participant’s response.
  - Failure to provide the information within 90 days results in denial.
- Denial notice contents (retirement claims):
  - Specific reasons for denial.
  - References to specific plan provisions relied upon.
  - Description of additional information needed and why.
  - Explanation of the plan’s claims review and appeal procedures.
  - Statement of right to bring a civil action under ERISA Section 502(a) after an appeal denial.
- Appeal rights and process (retirement claims):
  - Participant has 60 days from receipt of the denial to file a written appeal.
  - Participant may obtain, free of charge, all documents, records, and other information relevant to the claim.
  - Participant may submit additional comments, records, and information regardless of whether they were provided initially.
  - Committee conducts a full and fair review and issues a decision within 60 days; may extend up to a total of 120 days for special circumstances with timely written notice.
- Final appeal decision contents (retirement claims):
  - Specific reasons for the decision.
  - References to specific plan provisions relied upon.
  - Statement of the participant’s right to free access to relevant documents and records.
  - Statement of the right to bring a civil action under ERISA Section 502(a) after an appeal denial.
- Disability claims procedures:
  - Section 9.5 begins, indicating the Committee will provide notice of the status of a disability claim within a reasonable period after a complete claim is filed; further details are not included in the excerpt.
text: 4 Retirement Claims Procedures To the extent that a Participant’s claim relates to a determination with respect to his Accounts, other than a Disability determination, the Committee will provide the Participant with notice of the status of his claim for retirement benefits within a reasonable period of time after a complete claim has been filed, but no later than 90 days after receipt of the Participant’s benefit claim. The Committee may request an additional 90 day extension if special circumstances warrant by notifying the Participant of the extension before the expiration of the initial 90 day period. If the Participant has not submitted sufficient information to the Committee to process the Participant’s retirement benefit claim, the Participant will be notified of the incomplete claim and given 90 days to submit additional information. This will extend the time in which the Committee has to respond to the Participant’s claim from the date the notice of insufficient information is sent to the Participant until the date the Participant responds to the request. If the Participant does not submit the missing information to the Committee within 90 days of the date of the request, the claim will be denied. If the Participant’s benefit claim is denied, the Participant will receive a notice which will include: (i) the specific reasons for the denial, (ii) reference to the specific Plan provisions upon which the decision is based, (iii) a description of any additional information the Participant might be required to provide with an explanation of why it is needed, (iv) an explanation of the Plan’s claims review and appeal procedures, and (v) a statement regarding the Participant’s right to bring a civil action under Section 502(a) of ERISA following a denial on appeal. The Participant may appeal a denial of a retirement benefit claim by filing a written request with the Committee within 60 days of receipt of the initial denial notice. In connection with the appeal, the Participant may request thatthe Committee provide, free of charge, copies of all documents, records, and other information relevant to the claim. The Participant may also submit written comments, records, documents, and other in formation relevant to the appeal, whether or not such documents were submitted in connectio n with the initial claim. The Committee will conduct a full and fair review of the documents a nd evidence submitted and will ordinarily render a decision on the Participant’s benefit claim no later than 60 days after receipt of the request for review on appeal. If there are special circumstances, the decision will be made as soon as possible, but not later than 120 days after receipt of the request for review on appeal. If such an extension of time is needed, the Participant will be notified in writing prior to the end of the first 60 day period. 9.4 Retirement Claims Procedures To the extent that a Participant’s claim relates to a determination with respect to his Accounts, other than a Disability determination, the Committee will provide the Participant with notice of the status of his claim for retirement benefits within a reasonable period of time after a complete claim has been filed, but no later than 90 days after receipt of the Participant’s benefit claim. The Committee may request an additional 90 day extension if special circumstances warrant by notifying the Participant of the extension before the expiration of the initial 90 day period. If the Participant has not submitted sufficient information to the Committee to process the Participant’s retirement benefit claim, the Participant will be notified of the incomplete claim and given 90 days to submit additional information. This will extend the time in which the Committee has to respond to the Participant’s claim from the date the notice of insufficient information is sent to the Participant until the date the Participant responds to the request. If the Participant does not submit the missing information to the Committee within 90 days of the date of the request, the claim will be denied. If the Participant’s benefit claim is denied, the Participant will receive a notice which will include: (i) the specific reasons for the denial, (ii) reference to the specific Plan provisions upon which the decision is based, (iii) a description of any additional information the Participant might be required to provide with an explanation of why it is needed, (iv) an explanation of the Plan’s claims review and appeal procedures, and (v) a statement regarding the Participant’s right to bring a civil action under Section 502(a) of ERISA following a denial on appeal. The Participant may also submit written comments, records, documents, and other in formation relevant to the appeal, whether or not such documents were submitted in connectio n with the initial claim. The Committee will conduct a full and fair review of the documents a nd evidence submitted and will ordinarily render a decision on the Participant’s benefit claim no later than 60 days after receipt of the request for review on appeal. If there are special circumstances, the decision will be made as soon as possible, but not later than 120 days after receipt of the request for review on appeal. If such an extension of time is needed, the Participant will be notified in writing prior to the end of the first 60 day period. start_phrase: Determinations by the Comm ittee or Investment Committees and any interpretation, rule, or administrative decision adopted by t he Committee or Investment Committees shall be final and binding for all Plan purposes and upon all interested persons, their heirs, and their personal representatives.
summary:

text: Finality of Committee Determinations Determinations by the Comm ittee or Investment Committees and any interpretation, rule, or administrative decision adopted by t he Committee or Investment Committees shall be final and binding for all Plan purposes and upon all interested persons, their heirs, and their personal representatives. No action at law or in equity shall be brought to recover benefits under the Plan until the claim and review processes in this Section have been exercised and until the Plan benefits requested in such review have been denied in whole or in part. If any judicial proceeding is undertaken to appeal the denial of a claim or bring any other action under ERISA, other than a breach of fiduciary duty claim, the evidence presented shall be strictly limited to the evidence timely presented to the Committee. If the Committee denies a Participant’s appeal in whole or in part, and the Participant subsequently wishes to file a claim against the Plan, any such legal action must be brought within 120 days of the Committee’s final dec ision. title: Amounts Held in Grandfathered Accounts
heading: 11.1 Amounts Held in Grandfathered Accounts
start_phrase: In the eve nt that the stock or substantially all the assets of an Employer, its subsidiary, or one of its divisions is sold, or if a majority of the beneficial ownership of an Employer, subsidiary, or one of its divisions alters (“Change in Control”), the Grandfathered Accounts of Participants affected by such sale shall become immediately due and payable unless a successor of the Employer assumes the lia bilities and responsibilities relating to the affected Participants.
summary:
The excerpt outlines how participant accounts are treated upon a change in control:

- Section 11 sets payout/vesting rules triggered by corporate control changes.
- 11.1 (Grandfathered Accounts): If the Employer, a subsidiary, or a division experiences a sale of stock or substantially all assets, or a majority change in beneficial ownership, affected participants’ grandfathered accounts become immediately due and payable, unless a successor assumes all related liabilities and responsibilities.
- 11.2 (409A Accounts): If there is a change in ownership, effective control, or a substantial asset sale of the Employer as defined under IRC Section 409A, affected participants’ 409A accounts become 100% vested and are paid immediately in a lump sum.
- Key distinctions: 409A treatment follows IRS-defined “Change in Control Event” and mandates lump-sum payment and full vesting; grandfathered accounts trigger immediate payment but allow an exception if a successor assumes obligations.

summary:
- CEO (Ronald Delia) and CFO (Michael Casamento) certifications for Amcor plc’s Annual Report on Form 10-K under Exchange Act Rules 13a-14(a)/15d-14(a) (SOX 302).
- Each certifies they reviewed the report; it contains no untrue statements or material omissions; and the financial statements and other financial information fairly present, in all material respects, the company’s financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows for the periods presented.
- They assert responsibility for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and procedures and internal control over financial reporting (ICFR), including:
  - Designing disclosure controls to ensure material information from the company and its consolidated subsidiaries is made known to them.
  - Designing ICFR to provide reasonable assurance over reliable financial reporting and GAAP-compliant financial statements.
  - Evaluating and concluding on the effectiveness of disclosure controls as of period end.
  - Disclosing any changes in ICFR during the most recent fiscal quarter that materially affected or are reasonably likely to materially affect ICFR.
- They disclose to the auditors and audit committee:
  - All significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in ICFR.
  - Any fraud, whether or not material, involving management or employees with significant ICFR roles.
- Signed and dated August 27, 2020: Ronald Delia, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (Exhibit 31.1) and Michael Casamento, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer (Principal Financial Officer) (Exhibit 31.2).
text:
EXHIBIT 31.1
 
RULE 13a-14(a)/15d-14(a) CERTIFICATION OF CEO
 
I, Ronald Delia, certify that:
1. I have reviewed this Annual Report on Form 10-K of Amcor plc;
2. Based on my knowledge, this report does not contain any untrue state ment of a material fact or omit to state a material fact necessary to make the statements made, in light of the circumstances
under which such statements were made, not misleading with respec t to the period covered by this report;
3. Based on my knowledge, the financial statements, and other financ ial information included in this report, fairly present in all material  respects the financial condition, results of operations and
cash flows of the registrant as of, and for, the periods presented in this report;
4. The registrant’s other certifying officer(s) and I are responsible for e stablishing and maintaining disclosure controls and procedures (as  defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e))
and internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Exchange Ac t Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f)) for the registrant and have:
a) Designed such disclosure controls and procedures, or caused such disclo sure controls and procedures to be designed under our supervision, to ens ure that material information relating to
the registrant, including its consolidated subsidiaries, is mad e known to us by others within those entities, particularly during t he period in which this report is being prepared;
b) Designed such internal control over financial reporting, or caused su ch internal control over financial reporting to be designed under our supervis ion, to provide reasonable assurance
regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with genera lly accepted accounting principles;
c) Evaluated the effectiveness of the registrant’s disclosure control s and procedures and presented in this report our conclusions about the  effectiveness of the disclosure controls and
procedures, as of the end of the period covered by this report based on such eva luation; and
d) Disclosed in this report any change in the registrant’s internal  control over financial reporting that occurred during the registrant’s  most recent fiscal quarter (the registrant’s fourth fiscal
quarter in the case of an annual report) that has materially affected, o r is reasonably likely to materially affect, the registrant’s internal  control over financial reporting; and
5. The registrant’s other certifying officer(s) and I have disclosed, bas ed on our most recent evaluation of internal control over financial rep orting, to the registrant’s auditors and the audit committee
of the registrant’s board of directors (or persons performing the equivalen t functions):
a) All significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in the des ign or operation of internal control over financial reporting which are reaso nably likely to adversely affect the registrant’s
ability to record, process, summarize and report financial informati on; and
b) Any fraud, whether or not material, that involves management or other e mployees who have a significant role in the registrant’s internal  control over financial reporting.
Date August 27, 2020  /s/ Ronald Delia
Ronald Delia, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer
